title: A Aftermath for the Interior
premise: Marguerite Dunmore, a piano tuner who has spent ten years caring for her ailing mother and the crumbling family house in coastal Maine, has never asked why her father's will names a beneficiary she's never heard of. At her mother's funeral, a stranger named Elias Vann appears, calling the family by their original surname, Moreau, and claiming to be the son her brother gave up decades ago. As Marguerite tunes the house's ancient radiators and hears its history in their pipes, she and Elias uncover the secret the whole family arranged itself around: her father was not her father at all, and Elias is the proof. With the house about to be sold by her resentful brother, Marguerite must finally say the thing she's almost said for ten years — that she loves the house, and Elias, enough to claim them both. The novel ends with the siblings splitting the estate, Marguerite keeping the house, and Elias staying through one last winter to learn its sounds alongside her.
about_author: Ada Reyes grew up in a family of piano technicians in a drafty Victorian house on the Maine coast, where she learned to read rooms by their sounds before she could read words. Her fiction explores the quiet violence of things left unsaid in old families.

chapters.title: The Pitch of Empty Rooms
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. On the morning of her mother's funeral, Marguerite tunes the parlor piano to steady herself, listening through the radiators to the house's grief. At the service, a stranger introduces himself as Elias Vann and calls the family 'Moreau,' a name nobody uses. Her brother Robert goes white. The emotional beat is suppressed dread beneath ritual mourning — the almost-said question taking physical form.

chapters.title: What the Pipes Remember
chapters.summary: Alternating Marguerite and Elias POV. Elias stays at a local inn and begins visiting, ostensibly to settle the will; Marguerite shows him the house, and the radiators' hisses and knocks reveal to her that he already knows its layout. They discover a locked attic trunk with christening records under the Moreau name. Rising tension: Robert threatens to sell the house before probate ends, and Marguerite feels her ten years of silence collapsing.

chapters.title: A Name Nobody Uses
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. In the trunk, Elias finds letters proving Marguerite's father raised her knowing she was another man's child — Elias's grandfather's child, making Elias and Marguerite not cousins but something closer to siblings by blood and strangers by everything else. He confronts Robert, who confesses the family arranged its silences to protect an inheritance and an affair. Climax: the truth spoken aloud shatters the house's long-held pitch, and Robert signs the sale papers anyway.

chapters.title: Tuning
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. With the sale pending, Marguerite finally says the thing she has practiced for a decade: that the house is hers by care if not by blood, and she wants Elias to stay. Robert, hollowed by confession, agrees to split the estate instead of selling. The resolution lands in winter's first cold snap, Marguerite teaching Elias to listen to the radiators, the house retuning itself around two people who finally belong in it.
